summary: Lock refresh for TM-16's next action 'refresh the Python locks regularly'. No code change apart from VERSION 0.42.3 -> 0.42.4. router/requirements-lock.txt (what pydeps.py lets pip install into the router's venv on top of the distribution, --require-hashes --no-deps): paho-mqtt 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0, written by lock_requirements.py pin, which takes every SHA-256 PyPI publishes for the release; the two hashes equal those already in the container lock and the CI lock (compared), verify-pypi confirms them. paho-mqtt 2.2.0 (upstream changelog read) hardens packet parsing against corrupted and malformed packets, fixes keepalive and QoS 2 inflight tracking, drops Python 3.7/3.8 (the router needs 3.11) and turns two ValueErrors into TypeErrors for wrong argument types (max_queued_messages_set, callback_api_version). Traced B9: the only user is ha.py (MQTT to Home Assistant); new_client passes CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION1 as before and ha.py calls neither max_queued_messages_set nor reinitialise; a probe built the client with 2.2.0 (VERSION1, the same DeprecationWarning as 2.1.0) and set the callbacks ha.py uses. Traced B8: pydeps.plan installs a lock entry only where the venv lacks the package or holds a differing version it installed before; a distribution's own python3-paho-mqtt is untouched, the router image already installs 2.2.0 from its own lock (ADR-0121). requirements-ci-lock.txt, re-resolved on Linux with lock_requirements.py resolve in the router's pinned base image: ruff 0.17.4 -> 0.17.6, pydantic 2.14.3 -> 2.14.4, pydantic_core 2.50.4 -> 2.50.5, every other pin unchanged; these are installed in CI only (--require-hashes). hindsight-client stays 0.10.3: 1.x is outside the <1 bound of test/requirements-hindsight.txt, deliberately not moved here. pip-audit 2.10.1 (as in security.yml) finds no known vulnerability in any of the three locks.

tests.command: python tools/security/lock_requirements.py check ; python tools/security/lock_requirements.py verify-pypi
tests.evidence: Python locks: 0 problem(s); PyPI verification: 0 problem(s).
No known vulnerabilities found, for each lock.

run after staging this record; added lines are version pins, PyPI hashes and the changelog row.

limitations: paho-mqtt 2.2.0 was not run against a real MQTT broker; ha.py's client construction and callback API were probed, the network path is unchanged code.
The upstream changelog describes the hardening; the packet parser changes themselves were not audited.
Hosts keep their distribution's paho-mqtt; only venv installs from the lock change.
